headline: High risk: Cursor can feed untrusted workspace content into n8n workflows, creating dangerous prompt-injection and data-leak paths by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard contents, and can use MCP; n8n workflows can process arbitrary file/API inputs and invoke downstream nodes. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content from Cursor is handed into n8n as instructions or data without provenance tracking. The pair’s documented shared filesystem and broad tool surfaces make this more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Cursor content is copied or written into an n8n workflow input without provenance checks
IF n8n AI Agent or downstream nodes treat that content as instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic handoff from Cursor to n8n; require manual review of every payload.
Add a fixed delimiter/template that separates data from instructions.
Use a provenance tag or allowlist for fields accepted by n8n.
Turn off Cursor Yolo mode for any workflow-authoring session.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the integration boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can egress broadly to model providers and MCP servers. n8n processes whatever the workflow handles and can send data through many integration nodes. If sensitive workspace data is moved from Cursor into n8n, both agents can expose it to external services, creating a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files or clipboard contents are passed from Cursor into an n8n workflow
IF the workflow uses any external integration node or model provider
mitigations: Restrict both agents to a non-sensitive test workspace.
Disable clipboard-based transfer between Cursor and n8n.
Review n8n nodes for external egress before enabling the workflow.
Use separate credentials and accounts for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls at the workflow boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shell commands. Cursor also modifies git state, while n8n writes to the server filesystem and can run Execute Command. Their shared-state models differ, but overlapping write authority on connected systems creates a real conflict risk, especially if both touch the same repo or server-mounted workspace.
conditions: IF Cursor and n8n target the same repository or mounted directory
IF both are allowed to write or run commands concurrently
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory.
Disable concurrent writes during shared tasks.
Require git locks or a single-writer policy.
Avoid letting n8n run Execute Command on the same repo Cursor edits.
requires-engineering: add orchestration-level locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor can generate code, facts, and edits that n8n can then consume as workflow inputs or trigger actions through integrations. Because n8n is an orchestrator with tool-calling nodes, it may act on Cursor-produced output without independent verification. That makes a bad Cursor suggestion capable of cascading into automated downstream actions in n8n.
conditions: IF n8n uses Cursor-produced text, code, or JSON as authoritative workflow input
IF downstream n8n nodes execute actions without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before any n8n action.
Require schema validation on Cursor-generated payloads.
Limit n8n to read-only dry runs until outputs are verified.
Log and diff Cursor outputs before workflow execution.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates between generation and action.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that handles source code and clipboard contents, while n8n is a workflow server that processes whatever data the workflow touches and stores credentials on its server. If regulated data is routed from Cursor into n8n, retention, residency, or subject-rights obligations can diverge across the two systems. The profiles do not prove a specific breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data such as customer records or secrets is moved from Cursor into n8n
IF the n8n workflow stores or logs that data outside the required residency or retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workflow.
Review n8n retention and logging settings before use.
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated work.
Minimize credential scope in n8n integrations.
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls across both systems.
